# Feature — Enforce the post-deadline thrash gate at every local-dispatch entry; terminal in-request detour

Child of LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV. Implementation slice: after the deterministic tests
(C1) pin the mechanism, make the cancelled session's claim on the local gate end with
the cancellation — the thrash-cooldown gate engages for EVERY local dispatch attempt
(including paths that bypass provider.py's chain gate), the same request does not
re-dispatch local after the deadline detour, and any remaining lease is bounded
≤300 s.

## Target outcome

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` stops holding the local
dispatch gate: no in-request local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh lease ~150 ms after
the release; the per-session thrash cooldown demonstrably engages at every local
dispatch entry; `local_prefill_in_flight` never outlives the dispatch it marks; every
remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s (parent AC1-AC3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1. Every path that can acquire a local dispatch lease consults the per-session
  thrash cooldown before acquisition — including direct local paths that bypass
  provider.py's chain gate (the shape C1's isolation test surfaced). A session whose
  cooldown is armed is refused (`routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`)
  with the chain falling to the next provider. C1's gate-engagement test goes green.
  Rollback knob `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 0` still disables the gate.
- AC2. The deadline detour is terminal for local within that request: a request-scoped
  marker set on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` prevents the same request from acquiring a
  fresh lease after release (the ~150 ms post-release fresh lease is impossible). C1's
  re-dispatch test goes green.
- AC3. After the cancellation the lease, `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are cleared
  BEFORE any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill stream is closed (proven dead)
  so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker (no
  `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` after release). C1's marker test
  goes green.
- AC4. Any remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s from its last progress for every
  acquisition path (deadline detour, same-session re-acquisition, active-expired
  sweep) without weakening the 180 s no-progress watchdog or the 10 s sweep cadence.
  C1's bound test goes green.
- AC5. Legitimate long prefills are unaffected: a live, progressing prefill keeps its
  lease (no-preemption same-session semantics preserved); first-byte latency stays
  inside `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`; a successful local first byte clears
  the cooldown per the recovery-fraction rule (parent constraints).
- AC6. Changed-scope test gate passes and the full suite stays green with the fix.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken: the prefill deadline (120 s) detour-not-kill backstop, the
  no-progress watchdog (180 s), the 10 s sweep, the thrash cooldown (600 s / rollback
  knob 0), no-preemption same-session lease re-acquisition for genuine in-flight
  prefills.
- Scope: do NOT absorb lease-fairness renewal caps (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) — record any
  overlap as related work, keep that item's scope there.
- Fix the mechanism C1 identifies (bypass and/or arm-key mismatch); a renewal cap alone
  is insufficient if the gate remains unengaged (parent AC1 mandates an engaged gate).

## Risky assumptions

- The incident re-dispatch is a same-request/retry client pattern (pi/opencode retries
  on 503); the request-scoped marker must not block unrelated concurrent requests from
  the same session (the session cooldown covers those).
- Closing the upstream prefill stream is sufficient to prevent stale-marker
  re-extension (verify with C1's marker test).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a request-scoped post-deadline marker set in the `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
   path and checked at the lease-acquisition choke point; local is terminal for that
   request (chain falls to the next provider).
2. Consult the thrash cooldown at the single choke point every local dispatch passes
   (router.py `proxy_to_local` immediately before `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) so
   direct bypass paths engage; keep the existing provider.py gate.
3. Harden the release path (deadline + measured-abort twins) so record + marker
   removal and upstream-stream close (bounded by `disconnect_cleanup_timeout`) complete
   before any retry can observe stale state.
4. Update code comments at the changed sites; keep the existing log vocabulary
   (`routing_skip_local`, `lease_released`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`proxy_to_local`, `prefill_deadline_exceeded` block)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_extend_lease_during_prefill`)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (local branch + any direct dispatch paths C1 surfaces)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` (harness extended by C1)
- Related: `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (`_dispatch_local_model_load` direct
  `srv.proxy_to_local`), per C1's cause comment

# Load-normalise the AC3 denial check in the idle-admit measurement

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the AC3 `local_dispatch_denied` check normalised to
window load (per bypass/fallback event), so the measured `+9.3 %` per-hour
denial "increase" (window 2026-10-22 21:48 → 2026-10-23 21:48, ~2× busier than
the before window) is judged on a load-independent signal instead of a
confounded raw rate.

## Measured evidence (artifact `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `local_dispatch_denied` raw | 66.0 /h | 72.1 /h | **+9.3 %** (> 5 % band → fail) |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,790 | 3,702 | +107 % |
| Remote fallback events | 6,953 | 12,888 | +85 % |
| Denials per bypass+fallback event | 1,584/8,743 = 0.181 | 1,731/16,590 = 0.104 | −42 % |

The raw rate cannot distinguish "the override causes more denials" from "a 2×
heavier window produces proportionally more denials". The tool currently
implements only the raw per-hour rate (`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`:
`denied_before_rate`/`denied_after_rate`, `_DENIED_TOLERANCE_PCT = 5.0`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` reports a load-normalised denial rate — denials per bypass+fallback event — alongside the existing per-hour rate, in both the AC3 check and the JSON/markdown output.
- The AC3 verdict uses the normalised rate for pass/fail (the raw per-hour rate remains reported), so a raw increase caused purely by higher load no longer fails the check; a genuine per-event increase still fails.
- Tests cover: the normalised-rate arithmetic against the exact window numbers above (fail → pass), a synthetic per-event denial increase that still fails the check, and backward compatibility of all existing JSON keys and exit codes.
- Re-running the tool `--window-closed` on the closed window records the AC3 verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the baselines table, with the normalised numbers and sample counts.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` documents the normalised metric definition and why the raw per-hour rate is load-confounded.

## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# Test: local-preferred behaviour matrix

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

Pin the whole contract in one table-driven regression suite so future routing work cannot silently revert to "hard 429" or "silent remote".

## Matrix

| Preference | Slot | Verdict | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| absent / `prefer-local` | free | — | local (unchanged) |
| absent / `prefer-local` | busy | deferrable | remote fallback (unchanged) |
| `remote-ok` | — | — | local removed from chain, remote serves (unchanged) |
| `local-preferred` | free | — | local |
| `local-preferred` | busy | deferrable | queue → retryable 429, **no** remote dispatch |
| `local-preferred` | busy | too_large | remote serves, **no** local-capacity 429 |
| `local-only` (legacy) | busy | deferrable | identical to `local-preferred` |
| any | — | remote-less chain (`private` model) | unchanged |

## Deliverables

- Extend `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (rename semantics or add a sibling file) and `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` with the matrix above.
- Each row asserts: HTTP status, `X-Local-Route`, `X-Provider` / served entry, the presence or absence of remote dispatch (spy on `proxy_to_remote`), and for deferrals the retry fields.
- A named regression reproducing the 2026-10-28 incident numbers (`eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=6627`, `budget_tokens=25000`) asserting `deferrable` + retryable 429 + zero remote calls.

### Per-row assertion detail (makes AC1/AC4 decidable)

| Matrix row | Home | Additional assertions |
|---|---|---|
| absent / `prefer-local`, free | `test_admission_reserve.py` (vocabulary rows) + `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (existing exit rows) | `X-Local-Route: local`, local provider name in `X-Provider`, zero remote calls; response shape byte-identical to today (no `retryable`, no `verdict` field) |
| absent / `prefer-local`, busy, deferrable | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (existing exit rows) | remote provider serves, `X-Local-Route: remote`, local neither dispatched nor refused |
| `remote-ok`, any | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (`test_remote_ok_still_strips_local_entries`) | local entry absent from the resolved chain (`apply_local_preference` output), remote serves |
| `local-preferred`, free | `test_local_admission_guard.py` (`_free_slot_cfg`) | served locally, `X-Local-Route: local`, no queue entry, no 429 |
| `local-preferred`, busy, deferrable | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (preference axis on every exit row) + `test_local_admission_guard.py` | 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` set, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair, body verdict `deferrable`, **zero** `proxy_to_remote` calls |
| `local-preferred`, busy, too_large | `test_local_admission_guard.py` (`_cold_budget_cfg` + over-budget prompt) | remote serves, **no** 429, no `X-Local-Route: refused`, local removed from chain |
| `local-only` (legacy), busy, deferrable | `test_admission_reserve.py` (`parse_preference` row) + matrix rows above re-run under the alias | normalises to `local-preferred`; identical status/headers/retry fields to the `local-preferred` row, one deprecation log line per request |
| any, remote-less chain (`private`) | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (`no_local_route` row family) | deferral unchanged (retryable 429 per A5), never promoted, no remote entry to dispatch to |

## Dependency & sequencing

- Depends on LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (vocabulary), LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ (verdict) and LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE (chain/deferral). All three are still `open`/`blocked` as of the 2026-10-28 planning run, so this item stays `blocked` and is implemented **last** in the epic.
- Row expectations are *owned* by those three items: the verdict vocabulary (`deferrable` / `too_large`), the retryable-429 field names and headers, and the per-exit-path list all come from them. Re-read their descriptions and the landed code before writing assertions; do not re-derive the vocabulary here — import the production constants/helper so a rename in the owning item fails loudly in one place instead of drifting.
- Test-first ordering is satisfied at epic level: each prerequisite child lands its own tests with its slice (decision 2 in LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY). This item is the cross-cutting matrix that asserts *already-implemented* behaviour; writing it first would deadlock the dependency graph.

## Existing state (reuse, do not duplicate)

- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — `_ExitRow` table, one row per exit from the local route (`thrash_cooldown`, `router_skip_physical_cap`, `router_skip_economic`, `router_skip_residency`, `router_skip_tenancy`, `queue_depth_cap`, `queue_wait_expiry`, `admission_guard_free_slot`, `entry_context_cap`, `quota_hard_stop`, `chain_cooldown`, `no_local_route`), each a `pytest.param` asserting 429 + `X-Local-Route: refused` + `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` + no upstream call. Its module docstring already explains the matrix design and records that the `xfail(strict=True)` machinery was retired when the choke point landed.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — reserve/verdict unit rows plus the existing remote spy `patch("proxy.server.proxy_to_remote", _remote)` (≈ lines 443, 489, 530, 604, 642); `test_unknown_preference_value_falls_back_to_prefer_local` is the vocabulary row to extend.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — guard suite with `_guard_patches()`, `_free_slot_cfg()`, `_cold_budget_cfg()`, `_OccupancyRefusalCase`, `_RefusalContractRow` and `test_refusal_contract_table_has_exactly_one_row_per_reason`; the incident regression belongs beside these.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` — parses the documented retry contract (`_contract_rows()`, `_documented_timing()`) and already asserts `test_local_only_is_documented_as_refusal_not_remote_fallthrough`; new doc/contract assertions follow this shape.
- Spy hooks for "no remote dispatch": `patch("proxy.server.proxy_to_remote", ...)` at reserve level and `patch("proxy.provider._get_proxy_to_remote", ...)` at dispatch-loop level (pattern in `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold.py`).

## Reuse and implementation notes

- Reuse the exit-path table: add a **preference axis** (legacy `local-only` alias and `local-preferred`) to `_EXIT_ROWS` instead of restating the exits in a second table — a duplicated exit description is exactly the drift this matrix exists to catch.
- No rename of `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`: renaming breaks citations in `proxy/docs/routing.md`, sibling work items and the retry-docs assertions for no behavioural gain. Retitle its module docstring to "local-pinned refusal matrix (`local-preferred`, legacy `local-only` alias)".
- Tests must not re-implement the verdict or the ETA: call the production helper (`local_capacity_verdict(...)`, `evaluate_admission(...)`) and the production retry-timing helper and assert on their outputs. Only the incident regression pins literal numbers (taken from the 2026-10-28 log lines); every other row derives from config plus the calibrated seed.
- Every row is its own `pytest.param(..., id=...)` with row-specific expectation fields, so a red row names the behaviour that broke (AC1). # Docs: local-preferred semantics, wire compatibility and client migration

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY. Depends-on: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE (chain/deferral — the documented behaviour must be the shipped behaviour).

## Goal

Document the replacement of `local-only` by `local-preferred` everywhere an operator or client author looks, so an operator reading `proxy/docs/routing.md` or `proxy/config.yaml`, and a client author reading the retry contract, sees `local-preferred` as the canonical pin-local value and knows exactly what a retryable 429 asks of them.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/config.yaml` commentary for `X-Local-Preference` (the guard/reservation/preference block around `:1925`): describe the three effective behaviours (`prefer-local` default, `local-preferred` pin-with-deferral, `remote-ok` strip), the too-large promotion rule, and the counted-but-deprecated `local-only` alias.
- `proxy/config.yaml` `private` model comment (`:402-403`): state that a remote-less chain still defers (unchanged) and that `local-preferred` needs remote tiers to promote.
- The routing doc (`proxy/docs/routing.md` — the operator-facing routing document; root `README.md:267` points there and no separate `docs/local-admission*` file exists): add a short "local-preferred" section, the deferral/retry contract (retryable 429 with `Retry-After`/`retry_at`), the too-large promotion rule with its thresholds, and the 2026-10-28 incident shape as a worked example.
- Migration note: clients may keep sending `local-only`; the herdr/pi-extension rename is tracked in the ContextHub store; end-to-end deferral also needs the client to honour the retryable 429 (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7).
- Update stale documentation comments that describe `local-only` as the only local-pinning value (`admission_reserve.py`, `priority.py`, `provider.py` docstrings/comments).
- Move the prose assertion in `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` with the prose it pins (see AC6).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 No operator-facing doc or `config.yaml` comment still presents `local-only` as the primary/supported value without naming `local-preferred` as canonical. Verified by `grep -n "local-only" proxy/docs/routing.md proxy/config.yaml`: every remaining occurrence is in deprecated-alias context (states the alias is accepted and normalised).
- AC2 The deferral contract is documented with the exact 429 fields/headers a client must honour: status `429`, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, `retryable`, `Retry-After`, `retry_at` (RFC 3339 UTC), `suggested_action`, body `reason` plus body/header `new_tokens`/`budget_tokens` (`X-Local-Admission-New-Tokens` / `X-Local-Admission-Budget-Tokens`) and `X-Local-Admission*` estimate headers, and a body verdict of `deferrable`.
- AC3 The too-large promotion rule is documented with the thresholds it uses — `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (25000 new/uncached tokens) and the local context limit (`local_model_ctx_size`, per-slot effective context) — and states that a too-large prompt is never deferred and never refused for local capacity: the local entry leaves the chain and a remote tier serves it.
- AC4 Doc references to the ContextHub client items are accurate: epic WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0, herdr WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE, pi extension WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB, retryable-429 client handling WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 — each presented as client-side/out of scope for this repo, with the migration note stating that clients may keep sending `local-only`.
- AC5 Every related repo surface is updated: `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` (preference block + `private` note), and the stale `local-only`-as-the-only-pin docstrings/comments in `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`, `proxy/proxy/priority.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`. `proxy/README.md` requires no edit (it never names the header — see Existing state). No wiki or docs-site entry exists for this repo, so none is invented.
- AC6 The docs-contract test that pins this prose is updated in the same commit as the prose: `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` asserts the contract section says "refuse, not fall through" for `local-only`, so the rewritten section must carry a decidable equivalent for `local-preferred` (pinned while deferrable) and the assertion must be updated, not left passing on deleted wording.
- AC7 The 2026-10-28 incident is documented as a worked example with its logged shape — preference `local-only`, `local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct eta_prefill_s=31.7 eta_occupancy_s=31.7 projected_wait_s=63.4 budget_s=60.0 busy_slots=1`, `new_tokens=6627` against `budget_tokens=25000` — and the behaviour change it motivates (defer, then a retryable 429 with real retry timing; never a silent remote dispatch, never a terminal "All providers exhausted").
- AC8 The `private` model commentary states that a remote-less chain still defers (unchanged) and that `local-preferred` promotion to remote requires remote tiers in the chain.
- AC9 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-28)

- `proxy/docs/routing.md:1204` — `X-Local-Preference` table with `prefer-local` / `local-only` / `remote-ok` rows; `:1226` — per-reason retry contract (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) with its reason table; `:1270` — "Local-only means refuse, not fall through to remote" paragraph; `:1186` — "local-only preamble" refers to the `/reserve` `dry_run` idiom (unrelated sense; leave alone).

- `proxy/README.md` — no `X-Local-Preference` / `local-only` occurrence (grep, 2026-10-28); it links `docs/routing.md` at `:793`. `proxy/docs/routing.md` is therefore the only operator-facing routing surface.
- Stale docstrings/comments to refresh: `admission_reserve.py:56` (`PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`), `:78`, `:525`; `priority.py:415-416` ("``local-only`` and ``prefer-local`` keep the chain intact"); `provider.py` — 41 `local_only`/`local-only` occurrences, comments and docstrings only.
- `admission_reserve.py:98` — `local_only_no_local_route` is a **stable reason token** (LP-0MVRMC1W6003MV3Y), not prose: it must not be renamed by this docs pass.
- Unrelated-sense occurrences, out of scope: `handlers.py:557` / `:1016` (reservation "local-only preamble", `local_active_query` signal), `proxy_remote.py:174`, `router_helpers.py:1848` / `:1935` (the `local_active_query` counter), `proxy/test_home_page.py:42` / `:208` (a fixture provider literally named `local-only`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py:230` — `test_local_only_is_documented_as_refusal_not_remote_fallthrough` pins the "refuse, not fall through" prose (the only content-based assertion in that doc-contract suite).
- Historical records are not rewritten: `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md:37` / `:180` quote the header value as sent during a dated verification; AC1's operator-facing scope excludes dated analysis/verification records.

## Constraints

- **Docs-and-tests only.** No behaviour change, no config default change; the only test change is the prose assertion in AC6.
- **Document the shipped behaviour.** This item runs after LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE; if the landed implementation diverges from the parent description (e.g. a different deferral exit reason token, a different verdict field), document what shipped and record the divergence as a work-item comment, rather than re-specifying behaviour here.
- **No pre-emption of LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16.** The vocabulary child lands the table row and wire-compat note (and touches the `config.yaml` preference lines) first; this item refines the surrounding prose. Serial order avoids concurrent edits to the same lines.

It documents `local-only` as the enforced value; once this epic lands, that doc must present `local-preferred` (pinned while deferrable) as the value carrying the per-exit enforcement. ## Problem statement

When `implement.py finish` cannot fast-forward the main checkout to the commit it is
about to push (main checkout dirty from concurrent work), it logs a warning and pushes
anyway from that stale checkout. The `dev`/`main` push then runs `.githooks/pre-push`
with `--project-root <main checkout>` — so the full suite is measured against the *old*
working tree, and the result is cached under the *old* git-state fingerprint
(`HEAD` + dirty content). The push returns green in seconds without the pushed commit
ever being verified: a silent fail-open in the only full-suite enforcement point for
`dev`.

## Users

- **Agent implementers** running `implement.py finish` in a repo with a busy main
  checkout: they need a push that is either genuinely verified or loudly refused, never
  a green gate that proves nothing.
- **Producers / release reviewers** relying on `run_tests.py --summary` as the
  "the pushed commit was full-suite green" evidence trail.
- Example story: *As a producer reviewing a `dev` push, I want a green gate to mean the
  pushed commit's tree passed the full suite, so that I can trust `dev` without
  re-running the suite manually.*

## Acceptance criteria

- A `dev`/`main` push issued while the checked-out tree is **not** the pushed commit
  (dirty main checkout ⇒ skipped Step-5 fast-forward) either verifies the pushed commit
  itself or **fails closed**; it never reports green using evidence from a different
  tree.
- The gate's diagnostic (refusal message and/or finish output) names **both** the pushed
  commit (`local_sha`) and the tree/SHA actually under test, so the next operator knows
  which tree was verified.
- On the gated path, the suite run is keyed to the pushed commit (`run_tests.py
  --summary` reports a cached green entry at that commit), not to the stale checkout.
- A regression test reproduces "dirty main checkout + skipped fast-forward" in the
  existing hermetic hook sandbox and asserts the pushed commit is the tree under test
  (or that the push is refused), while the existing green `dev`-push test still passes.
- At least one test/validation criterion is covered by the repo suite; all related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and
  any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary (open — see Q1).** The observable defect spans two owners:
  the repo-local hook + its tests (this repo, `projects/llm`) and the framework
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` Step 5/6, canonical hook copies
  in `projects/SorraAgents`). Framework/agent-infrastructure files may not be edited
  without explicit authorisation; the default scope here is the repo-local hook and its
  regression test, with the framework change recorded as a linked follow-up.
- `.githooks/pre-push` must stay POSIX `sh` with no new runtime dependencies (it runs
  inside `git push` for every consumer of this repo).
- Feature-branch pushes must keep skipping the suite (fast loop unchanged) — the guard
  applies only to `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/heads/main` targets.
- The existing escape hatches (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, `--no-verify`) keep working.
- Cache plumbing stays fail-soft: mirroring must never decide a push's outcome.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` already reads all four stdin fields per pushed ref
  (`local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`) but uses only `remote_ref`; `local_sha`
  is discarded, so the gate cannot tell which commit it is supposed to verify.
- The gate runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`
  with `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — i.e. the checkout `git push`
  runs in, which `implement.py finish` makes the **main checkout**.
- `test_cache.compute_git_state()` fingerprints `HEAD` + the content of every dirty path,
  so a stale-but-dirty main checkout produces a *valid, different* fingerprint; a
  previous green run for that same stale+dirty state is a legitimate cache hit → the gate
  returns green in seconds.
- `implement.py` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new commit
  precisely so the hook sees the new files; on failure it only logs
  `"Fast-forward dev failed (%s); push will proceed from the stale checkout — the
  context-budget gate may reject the push."` and continues to Step 6
  (`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`).
- Observed 2026-10-28 (LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND): main checkout dirty (8 unrelated paths),
  fast-forward skipped, main `dev` stayed at `7393ef14`, push landed `11870e99`; gate
  green in seconds; `run_tests.py --summary` reported `missing` for the pushed commit;
  a throwaway worktree at the pushed commit gave 6136 passed / 0 failed.
- Existing coverage: `tests/test_git_hooks.py` (13 hermetic sandbox tests, fake runner,
  behavioural assertions) — its `_hook()` helper always sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`, so
  no test can express "pushed commit ≠ checked-out tree".

## Desired change

Gate the pushed commit, not "whatever is checked out". Two acceptable shapes (the
author's acceptance criteria allow either; see Q2 for the recommendation):

1. **Fail closed (preferred default).** In the `dev`/`main` gate block, compare
   `git rev-parse HEAD` in the gate's project root with the gated `local_sha`. On
   mismatch, refuse the push with an actionable message naming the pushed commit, the
   checked-out SHA, the tree path, and the recovery instructions (re-run
   `implement.py finish` once the main checkout is clean, or verify the commit in a
   worktree and re-push). Never execute the suite for the wrong tree.
2. **Gate the pushed commit itself.** Check out `local_sha` into a throwaway detached
   worktree and run the suite with `--project-root <worktree>`, mirroring the cache entry
   back (the hook already has `mirror_suite_cache`). Unblocks concurrent work at the cost
   of worktree lifecycle inside a hook.

Either way, the diagnostic must name the tree measured, and `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` must
describe the behaviour with a copy-pasteable reproduction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — capture the gated `local_sha` per `refs/heads/dev|main` ref in
  the stdin loop (currently discarded), then guard/redirect the gate; extend the
  refusal message; reuse `mirror_suite_cache` if option 2 is chosen.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — add a `local_sha` override to `_hook()` (reuse `_sandbox`,
  `_install_runner`, `_marker`); new regression test "stale checkout ≠ pushed commit is
  refused / gated against the pushed commit"; assert the fake runner is not invoked for
  the stale tree.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — document pushed-commit verification, the refusal, the
  `run_tests.py --summary` verification step, and the dirty-main-checkout reproduction.
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — no change expected (it only sets `core.hooksPath` and
  fixes the exec bit); confirm it stays a no-op for the new logic.
- Framework follow-up (only if Q1 authorises it — outside this repo):
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (Step 5 fast-forward ~5141–5216,
  Step 6 push ~5235, finish report), `~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py::compute_git_state`,
  and the canonical hook copies in `~/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 — "Investigate: dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong
  tree on the non-fast-forward retry path" (open, bug).** *Partial overlap — duplicate
  check performed.* Its AC1 already states the general invariant ("a mismatch between
  the push cwd's `HEAD` and the pushed `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong
  tree: gate it correctly or refuse with an actionable message") and AC3/AC4 require
  observable gate evidence plus a `HEAD` ≠ pushed-sha regression test. This item owns the
  **skipped-fast-forward / dirty-main-checkout** trigger and its concrete reproduction;
  the two triggers want the *same* hook guard, so implementing both separately would
  duplicate the fix (see Q2).
- LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9's discovering item: LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND (post-push verification
  surfaced the gap).
- LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ — "Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout
  (`core.hooksPath` unset)" — the gate's activation history and the same
  `run_tests.py --summary` = `missing` signal.
- LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK — activated `core.hooksPath` and pinned the context-budget
  thresholds (the gate family this item hardens).
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — the gate's contract, escape hatches and the
  "simulate a `dev` push" recipe.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (framework) — `implement.py finish` pushes from the
  main checkout by design; the reason a worktree-push alternative needs authorisation.

## Risks & assumptions

- *Risk: fail-closed blocks routine finishes* on hosts where the main checkout is
  routinely dirty (this host, 2026-10-28). Mitigation: the refusal message names the
  one-step recovery, and option 2 (gate in a worktree) is available. Assumption: a
  fail-closed push is acceptable engineering behaviour for a release gate.
- *Risk: HEAD equality alone is not enough* — a clean-HEAD but dirty tree still measures
  a tree that differs from the pushed commit (an uncommitted edit can mask a red
  commit). Open question Q3.
- *Risk (option 2): worktree creation inside a pre-push hook* can deadlock with
  `implement.py`'s own worktree lifecycle and doubles checkout/dependency handling.
- *Risk: scope creep into the framework.* Extra opportunities (finish-report wording,
  pushing from the worktree, propagating the guard to every consumer repo's hook copy)
  are recorded as linked follow-up items, not folded into this item.
- *Assumption: the cache fingerprint semantics stay as-is* (HEAD + dirty content);
  the gate must work with them rather than redefining the cache key.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Evidence gathered before asking (so the questions are not repo-search answerable):
`.githooks/pre-push` discards `local_sha`; `test_cache.compute_git_state()` keys on
`HEAD` + dirty content; `implement.py` Step 5 only *warns* when the fast-forward is
skipped and still pushes from `repo_root`; `tests/test_git_hooks.py::_hook()` always
sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`; the main checkout of this repo is currently clean.

- **Q1 (shape + scope).** Which fix shape, in which repository?
  - A: repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push` — refuse a `dev`/`main` push
    when the checkout's `HEAD` ≠ the gated `local_sha`, naming both SHAs, the tree path
    and the recovery step; regression test in `tests/test_git_hooks.py`; framework
    improvement filed as a linked follow-up.
  - B: repo-local "gate the pushed commit" — check out `local_sha` in a throwaway
    detached worktree inside the hook, run the suite with `--project-root <worktree>`,
    mirror the cache entry (`mirror_suite_cache`) so the entry lands at the pushed
    commit.
  - C: framework change only (`implement.py`: push from the worktree / verify the pushed
    commit / name the verified tree in the finish report) — requires explicit
    authorisation to edit agent-infrastructure files, tracked under a SorraAgents item.
  - **Recommended:** A — smallest deterministic change, testable in the existing hermetic
    sandbox, no worktree lifecycle inside a git hook, and it composes with B or C later
    (the guard is the invariant; B/C are the unblocking refinements).
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q2 (overlap with LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3).** That open item already requires "`HEAD` ≠
  pushed `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong tree" for the non-fast-forward
  retry path; this item's guard would satisfy both. Consolidate, or keep two items?
  - A: transfer this item's distinct ACs (dirty-main-checkout reproduction test;
    cache entry keyed to the pushed commit) onto LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 and close this item
    as a duplicate.
  - B: keep both, implement the shared guard once under whichever is scheduled first, and
    record a `Blocks`/related link so the second becomes verification only.
  - **Recommended:** B — the triggers are distinct regression scenarios (retry path vs
    dirty checkout) worth naming in tests, but only one implementation should exist.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q3 (strictness).** When `HEAD` *does* equal the pushed `local_sha` but the tree is
  dirty (foreign edits, untracked files), should the gate still run?
  - A: yes — run it, but warn loudly that the tree is not the pushed commit.
  - B: refuse — a dirty tree's fingerprint can never match the pushed commit's clean
    fingerprint, so `run_tests.py --summary` at the pushed commit stays `missing` and the
    evidence trail (AC3) is unmet.
  - **Recommended:** B, excluding any project-declared expected-dirty paths (none are
    declared for this repo); the main checkout is clean at intake time, so a clean-tree
    precondition is not a routine blocker here.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3** – Investigate: dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the non-fast-forward retry path (open)
- **LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ** – Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout (core.hooksPath unset) (completed)
- **LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK** – Install the .githooks/pre-push gate (core.hooksPath) so the dev-push full-suite gate actually runs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs (+358 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs (+358 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs (+358 more)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the proxy usage report (and any gate or alert that quotes a
"busy" percentage), I want the **non-GPU, log-derived local busy time**
(`dispatch → finish` slot union) used as *the* local model utilisation figure, so
that decisions are made on proxy-measured slot occupancy rather than on the
power-based hardware `GPU busy` proxy, which counts GPU activity the proxy does
not serve and therefore overstates local model utilisation.

## Context

The 2026-10-27/28 24h report (window 2026-10-27 22:10 → 2026-10-28 22:10) shows
the two figures diverging by ~27 points:

- Local busy, log-derived (`local_busy`, `dispatch → finish`): **12.6%** (3h 01m of 24h)
- Decode-only lower bound: 5.8% (1h 23m)
- Prefill busy: 1h 37m
- GPU busy, power-based (`gpu_busy`, Prometheus `gpu:computing:bool`, >= 90 W): **39.3%** (9h 26m)

The CLI stdout summary and several operator-facing artefacts lead with the
power figure, and LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG ("Gate: verify 60% local busy night")
phrases its precondition/AC0 as ">60% GPU busy" while its AC1 quotes the
report's `## Local model utilization` section — i.e. the gate mixes the two
definitions. `REFERENCE.md` already documents the log union as the *primary*
figure and the power row as a supplementary hardware-side signal, so the code
and the gates have drifted from the documented intent
(LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4 added the power row, LP-0MVJN9H2I00116FP defined
dispatch→finish).

**Assumption (recorded for review):** the requested change is to make the
non-GPU calculation the one consumed by decisions and headline reporting
(stdout summary, gate/AC wording, any threshold comparisons), *not* to remove
the power-based row — it stays as clearly-labelled supplementary hardware
telemetry. If the intent was instead "drop the GPU power row entirely",
adjust AC1/AC2 accordingly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Every decision-facing "busy %" in the report and its JSON summary is the log-derived `local_busy` (`dispatch → finish`); the power-based `gpu_busy` value remains available but is never presented as the local utilisation figure (it is labelled `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` and carries an explicit "not local model utilisation" note).
- AC2: The CLI stdout summary states the log-derived busy percentage as the local busy figure and, when `gpu_busy` is present, reports it separately with a label that distinguishes hardware activity from served local work.
- AC3: LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG's precondition/AC0 wording is corrected to quote the log-derived `local_busy` (documented via a comment on that item; this item does not change its status).
- AC4: `REFERENCE.md` states which busy figure is authoritative for decisions, when to prefer each, and why the two differ (log gaps, unfinished streams, GPU work outside the proxy's slot accounting) — matching the code.
- AC5: A regression test asserts that the summary/JSON busy figure used for decisions is the log-derived one and that `gpu_busy` remains a separate, clearly-labelled key (fixtures from real log lines, no live Prometheus dependency).
- AC6: A re-run of the analysis for the same 24h window produces the log-derived 12.6% figure in the decision-facing position, with the power figure still visible but no longer leading.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — summary section, `summary_to_json`, `_gpu_busy_json`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — stdout summary (`--json`, busy line)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` — power-based computation (unchanged, supplementary)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — busy definitions and interpretation

## Related

- LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4 (added the power-based GPU busy row)
- LP-0MVJN9H2I00116FP (defined `dispatch → finish` busy)
- LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG (60% local busy gate — wording to correct)
- discovered-from: proxy usage analysis report run, window 2026-10-27 22:10 → 2026-10-28 22:10

## Goal (user story)

As the operator of the LLM proxy, I want a 24 h post-deploy measurement proving the contended-pricing fix (parent LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3, AC4) drops the abandoned-queue-wait share below the 85 % baseline without new post-acceptance evictions — measured deterministically at the exact moment the window elapses, so the epic can close.

## Context

Parent AC4: "Post-change, the share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` drops below the 85 % baseline measured 2026-10-19/20 over a 24 h window, with no new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events."

- The contended-pricing fix was **deployed on 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC** (proxy restart, pid 1081749; code = local `dev` HEAD `52085f09` (committed 2026-10-29 00:07:08 UTC, i.e. before the restart), which contains the contended rate bucket `cc840d3d`, occupant-remaining rebase `91eab34d`/`9a866fc7`, baseline harness `a843e62c`, docs `323fe680`, decision-log/report surface `bb4bcb3c`).
- **Runnable at/after 2026-10-30 00:10 UTC** (24 h of post-deploy traffic).
- Pre-change baseline committed by the baseline child: `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion.{md,json}` (24 abandoned / 65 queued waits = 36.9 % abandoned share; per-band conversion table).
- Consumes the harness from the pre-change measurement child and the extended report from the parser child.

## Scope

- Capture a 24 h post-deploy window through `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (per-band conversion + abandoned-wait shares) and the proxy-usage-analysis report.
- Sanity gate before the verdict: the window must contain at least one `rate_bucket=contended`/`solitary_fallback` admission (proves the deployed code is actually pricing contended admissions) — if the bucket is still all `unknown`, the deployment did not take and the window is void.
- Compute the queued-local-wait share ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` and compare against the 85 % baseline and against the pre-change window.
- Count `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events in the window and triage any occurrences into an explanation or a follow-up item.
- Commit the measurement record (`docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.{md,json}`), labelled with the deploy hash (`52085f09`, local `dev` HEAD at restart) and window bounds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The post-change window's share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` is below 85 % (parent AC4) — or, if it is not, a follow-up work item is created recording the failure with the numbers.
- AC2: Zero new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events in the window, or every occurrence is explained and links to a triage item.
- AC3: The committed record shows the pre-change and post-change windows side by side (per-band conversion, abandoned shares, count of local admissions), with the AC verdict and the deployed commit hash (`52085f09`).
- AC4: The record is produced by the committed tools (no one-off analysis), reproducing the exact numbers without manual steps for the named logs; the window's `rate_bucket` distribution is reported (must not be all `unknown`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (from the baseline child)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion.md` + window JSON (pre-change baseline)
- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` + window JSON (this item's record)

## Dependencies

- Pre-change baseline + harness child (terminal); contended rate bucket child (terminal); occupant-remaining rebase child (terminal); parser/report child (terminal); **deploy = proxy restart performed 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC (completed)**.
- Supersedes LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA (the original time-blocked AC4 item, currently open and detached from the parent); this item carries the concrete runnable schedule.

## Deployment verification (2026-10-29 00:13 UTC)

Restart completed 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC (proxy pid 1081749, `/health` =
`healthy`, llama-server + TTS healthy). The contended-pricing code is provably
serving: `local_admission_guard` decision lines written after the restart carry
the new fields, e.g.

```
00:13:02 local_admission_guard decision=admit reason=within_budget ... eta_prefill_s=3.7 eta_occupancy_s=18.1 projected_wait_s=21.8 rate_bucket=solitary_fallback contended_samples=1 busy_slots=1 ...
```

(`rate_bucket` is `solitary_fallback` because the contended window has only 1
sample — below `local_admission_guard_min_samples` — which is the documented
"never price from a guess" behaviour. `eta_occupancy_s` (18.1 s) is now priced
above `eta_prefill_s` (3.7 s), i.e. the occupant-remaining term is live.)
Before the restart every decision logged `rate_bucket=unknown`, so this is a
hard before/after signal for AC4.

## Timing

- **Window opens:** 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC (restart).
- **Runnable from:** 2026-10-30 00:10 UTC (24 h of post-deploy traffic) —
  recommended `--since "2026-10-29 00:10:18" --until "2026-10-30 00:10:18"`.
- **Run before:** 2026-11-02 00:10 UTC (3 days), otherwise log rotation may
  drop the earliest part of the window.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator evaluating the 60 s → 30 s contention-queue sweep
(LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R), I want a windowed report that separates ticket-backed
dispatches, residual queue wins and residual queue losses (with a lease-active
`reason` split), so the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline and the post-flip verdict are
measured with one definition.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC3 (residual-queue telemetry) and
the AC1 trigger precondition (a ≥24 h baseline at 60 s / depth 8 must exist
before the sweep is applied).

## Scope

- New `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py`: CLI with `--log-dir`, a
  stated window (`--since`/`--until` or `--hours`), `--sweep-budget-seconds`
  (default 30), `--json` and a human/markdown render; modelled on
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`.
- Reuse `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (`discover_proxy_log_files`,
  `parse_line_timestamp`, `iter_proxy_log_lines`) and import
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a **read-only**
  library where practical (never edit that skill's files).
- Report sections for the window:
  (a) ticket-backed dispatches — `local_admission_reserve_claimed` count
      (reported, **not** a flip gate);
  (b) residual queue wins — `contention_queue_dispatch ... queued_duration=`,
      count, share at or below the sweep budget, and a wait distribution
      (p50/p75/p90/max);
  (c) residual queue losses — `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue ...
      queued_duration=`, count, aggregate wait, wait-per-hour, and a split by
      `reason` (`local_lease_active` vs `none`/other).
- Only the two lease-retention emit sites carry `reason=local_lease_active`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` ~12312 and ~12358); a missing `reason=` is
  counted as `none`, never dropped.
- Exit codes mirror `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`: 0 = measurement complete,
  2 = incomplete (no logs / thin window / coverage gap; never silently pass),
  1 = invalid input.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py --log-dir <dir> --hours 24`
   prints a report containing all three sections (ticket-backed count, win
   count/share/distribution, loss count/aggregate wait/reason split) for the
   stated window; `--json` emits the same numbers machine-readably.
2. Unit tests in `tests/test_contention_queue_sweep_report.py` drive the CLI
   against synthetic proxy-log fixtures (mixed wins/losses, lease-active and
   reason-less losses, empty window, window filtering) and assert every
   section, the reason split, the at-or-below-budget share, and the 0/2/1 exit
   codes — no live logs required.
3. The report is run against the available ≥24 h pre-flip window at 60 s /
   depth 8 and its numbers (queue events/h, wins, losses, aggregate dead wait,
   lease-active vs none split, ticket count) are recorded as a comment on this
   item and summarised on LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R.
4. A short runbook `docs/dev/contention-queue-sweep.md` documents the
   invocation, the three sections, the exit codes and the baseline numbers.
5. Changed-scope tests for the new script and its log parsing pass.

## Constraints

- Log events are the telemetry contract: **no new status counters**
  (`LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` removed the cumulative ones on purpose).
- Read-only use of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`; that skill is not edited.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (new)
- `tests/test_contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (new)
- `docs/dev/contention-queue-sweep.md` (new)
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (reuse: discovery + timestamps)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (read-only import)

## Dependencies

- None upstream.
- Its baseline must be recorded before the sweep child is applied (parent AC1
  trigger: ≥24 h 60 s / depth 8 baseline).

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the contention queue to be a bounded straggler net
(30 s, depth 2) instead of a 60 s parking lot, so dead local wait stops
competing with real local work, while a slot that frees within seconds is
still usable.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC2 (single-source budget) and
AC4 (tests/validation).

## Change

```yaml
contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30   # was 60 (was 120 in LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO)
contention_queue_max_depth: 2           # was 8
```

Evidence (proxy.log*, 2026-10-22 19:00→22:18, 3.3 h at 60 s / depth 8): 180
queue events — 38 wins (21 %) / 142 losses (79 %), every loss at the full
60 s, 8 705 s aggregate dead wait; wins retained by budget: 20 s → 24 %,
30 s → 34 %, 45 s → 60 %. Trigger, flip criteria and the two-line rollback
live on the parent item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `proxy/config.yaml` ships 30 s / depth 2 and the surrounding comment block
   (~lines 1740-1800) records the new evidence, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline
   requirement, the 7-day observation window, the three flip criteria and the
   two-line rollback (revert to 60 / 8, restart the proxy).
2. One resolver, tested end to end: `prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds(merged
   config, "medium") == 30.0`; the admission guard's refusal payload and
   `X-Local-Admission-Budget` header report 30 s; `POST /llama/local/reserve`
   prices against the same 30 s — all resolved through
   `_get_contention_queue_config` (no second constant, no per-call default).
   `high` priority still resolves to 0 s.
3. depth 2 is accepted unchanged; clamping happens only outside [1, 16]
   (values 1 and 16 pass through unchanged).
4. Queue behaviour at the swept caps: with 2 waiters parked, a third waiter
   falls back immediately without enqueueing; a parked waiter that is not
   served falls back at 30 s (tiny/mocked caps — never a real 30 s sleep).
5. Stale fixtures/tests that assert the shipped 60 s / 8 defaults are updated
   (`proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py::test_{cheap,fast}_config_declares_queue_policy`
   and any other shipped-config assertions), not left stale. The code-level
   defaults for a missing key stay as the inert no-config fallback and are
   documented as such (absent queue key ⇒ policy `fallback` ⇒ nothing queues).
6. Code comments in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (module docstring still says
   60 s), `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` and `proxy/proxy/router.py`
   state the single-budget contract; no behavioural change beyond the two
   config values.

## Constraints

- Fail-open semantics of the admission guard are unchanged (uncalibrated ⇒
  admit).
- One budget, one resolver: no new knob, no per-reason budget.
- Out of scope: queue removal, slot count, ctx-size, the ETA guard's model,
  client reservation adoption (`WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`).
- The config change requires a proxy restart; deployment happens in the
  observation child after a quiet-window restart, not in this item's session.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on the report/baseline child: the ≥24 h 60 s / depth 8 baseline must
  be recorded before this sweep is applied.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
2. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
3. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
4. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

## Goal

As an implementer of the GPU telemetry slices (parent LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W) I need
shared, deterministic verification assets — `/slots` payload fixtures, recorded
Prometheus HTTP API payloads, and a `gpu_busy_percent` guard that also covers the
new CLI — so every later child starts from a failing test instead of from code.

## Context

This is the **test-first slice** of the parent plan. It changes no production
behaviour: it delivers the verification harness that the sampler (sibling
"Publish slot occupancy metrics from the proxy"), the recording rule (sibling
"Combined computing-workload recording rule") and the CLI (sibling
"`gpu_utilisation` CLI with honest unknown share") consume.

Live evidence gathered while planning (2026-10-29, this host): the deployed
llama.cpp build answers `GET :8080/slots?model=mxbai-embed` with
`[{"id":0,"n_ctx":256,"speculative":false,"is_processing":false}, ...]` — no
`id_task` and no `next_token` while idle. Fixtures must therefore cover both this
build's shape and the older/richer shape that carries `id_task`/`next_token`.
`curl localhost:8000/slots` returns 404 (the proxy does not expose `/slots`), as
the parent brief states.

## Minimal implementation

- Add fixtures next to the tests that use them (`proxy/tests/`, pytest `conftest.py`
  or a small `gpu_fixtures.py` helper) — payload builders, not golden blobs, so a
  case is one keyword argument away.
- Record Prometheus API payloads as JSON under `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` with a
  small README line saying how each was captured (endpoint + query + window).
- Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` scanning in
  `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` to include `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reusable fixtures exist for a healthy `/slots` payload (mixed `is_processing`), an empty payload, a richer payload carrying `id_task`/`next_token`, and failed fetches (HTTP 500, timeout, connection error) — each fixture is asserted to have the shape its consumer expects.
- [ ] Recorded `query_range` payloads exist under `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` for `gpu:computing:bool`, `gpu:computing_workload:bool`, `gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` and `up{job="llama-proxy"|"node-exporter"}`, including one stream with a deliberate gap of missing samples; each file documents the endpoint, query and window it was captured from.
- [ ] The `gpu_busy_percent` guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` also scans `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` and fails if the series appears in any query expression, while still allowing documentation/comment mentions.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that the guard fails on a synthetic expression containing `gpu_busy_percent` and passes on the real files (the guard must not be vacuously green).
- [ ] Every test asserts observable behaviour (fixture shape, guard outcome, exact split), not merely that a value is non-`None`.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/conftest.py` / `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` (new or extended)
- `monitoring/tests/fixtures/slots_api_responses.json` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_telemetry_sampler.py` (fixture consumers land here later)

## Notes

Keep this slice small: only fixtures and guards that at least one sibling child
actually consumes. If a sibling ends up needing a different shape, extend the
fixture in that child rather than pre-building speculative variants.

# Drift guard: resolved full-suite command set must include hidden skill tests

## Goal

An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the resolved full-suite command set
includes a command targeting `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, so a
future configuration or resolution change cannot silently re-blind the
dev-push gate (parent AC5).

## Context

Parent: **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X** — repo full-suite gate never runs
`.pi/skills/*/tests` (529 unenforced tests).

**Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store, SorraAgents): upstream
`run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands()` must emit an extra explicit-path pytest
command for project-local skill test directories. This child lands the guard
that would have caught the original gap; it must not start before the upstream
rule is installed, because the assertion is red until then.

## Minimal implementation

- New `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`; resolve the runner exactly like
  `.githooks/pre-push`: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first,
  then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- Import the resolved module with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and
  call `full_suite_commands(REPO_ROOT)` — no nested suite execution.

# Fingerprint-scoped cooldown with free-GPU release

## Summary

Narrow the post-deadline prefill-thrash cooldown so it refuses only the
re-dispatch it was armed for, and release it when the proxy's own fresh snapshot
proves the GPU free.

Parent: LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB — AC2. Implementation item paired with the cooldown
scope regression test (its prerequisite).

## Target outcome

Zero `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` skips while the GPU is
demonstrably free (baseline 336 of 916 skips, 46 sessions, 241 for `herdr-*`),
while a re-dispatch of the failing prompt is still refused on every dispatch
path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — A cooldown armed by one abandonment must not veto local routing
  while the GPU is demonstrably free** (parent LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB AC2,
  restated as this item's outcome).

- The cooldown window is keyed by **(session, prompt fingerprint)**, not by
  session alone, so an unrelated — usually much smaller — prompt from the same
  session is no longer vetoed. The fingerprint is derived from the request
  payload at **both** the arming site and the gate site; when a usable
  fingerprint is unavailable at either site the gate **fails open to today's
  session-wide behaviour for that request** (never silently stops engaging).
- A re-dispatch of the failing prompt is still refused, on **every** local
  dispatch entry the code has today, with the existing
  `routing_skip_local … reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` contract (reason string,
  `cooldown_remaining_seconds`, retry/fallback contract unchanged). No dispatch
  entry loses the gate.
- A **free-GPU release** clears the window when, at gate time, the proxy's own
  snapshot is fresh (`slots_detail_stale=false`), shows no live dispatch
  (`local_in_flight_requests=0`), and holds no abandoned-but-processing slot;
  the release is logged with an attributable reason (e.g.
  `prefill_thrash_cooldown_released reason=free_gpu`). A stale snapshot, a live
  dispatch or an abandoned processing slot **never** releases the window.
- The existing clearing mechanisms are preserved: expiry, a comparable-size
  successful first byte (`local_prefill_thrash_recovery_fraction`,
  LP-0MVQITN6P008DPLB), and the `0` rollback knob which still disables arming
  *and* skipping.
- The intent of LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL is preserved: the 41-local-POST thrash
  scenario (same session, same large prompt, repeated after a deadline) stays
  suppressed. Asserted by the prerequisite regression test.
- Cross-session isolation is unchanged; the window store stays in-process and
  is reset with the rest of the routing state.
- Gate engagement regression: the `LP-0MVSAM2AV0077UAE` /
  `LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY` "gate engages at every dispatch entry" coverage is not
  touched — their engagement test is run as a regression and stays green
  (those items are re-measured, not absorbed here).
- The prerequisite regression test goes green and the full suite passes.
- The full project test suite passes with the change, run through the test
  skill (parent AC6; the dev-push gate enforces the full suite).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/router_helpers.py`: replace `_prefill_thrash_cooldowns: dict[str, float]`
  with a `(session_id, fingerprint)`-keyed store (plus the armed token size per
  key); update `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining`, `_clear_prefill_thrash_cooldown`,
  `_reset_prefill_thrash_cooldowns`, and add a
  `_release_prefill_thrash_cooldown_on_free_gpu` helper.
- `proxy/router.py`: pass the prompt fingerprint when arming (the request body
  is in scope on both the deadline and the measured-cache-deficit branches).
- `proxy/provider.py`: pass the fingerprint to the gate, and add the free-GPU
  release check using the same fresh-snapshot evidence the admission path
  already reads — after the gate decision, before queuing, so a released window
  never queues for a slot it cannot use.
- Keep the log line contract and add the release/skip evidence fields the
  measurement tool needs (additive `extra` fields only).

## Deliverables

- Fingerprint-scoped store, free-GPU release, unchanged gate engagement.
- The Appendix decisions it implements recorded on the parent item
  (fingerprint + release-on-free-GPU, chosen over a size band).

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Regression test: cooldown scope and free-GPU release** (test
  first).
- Depends on **Abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel on abandonment**:
  a "GPU shows free" release is only sound once abandoned work is excluded from
  the capacity signal (parent risk note: implement AC1 first).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — cooldown store + helpers
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — arming sites (deadline, measured cache deficit)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — local-branch gate
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_cooldown.py` — the prerequisite test
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` — regression
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline.py` — regression

# Add cooldown-skip metrics to capacity verification tool

## Summary

Make the cooldown-skip evidence re-derivable by the same tool that produces the
capacity numbers, by adding `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`
metrics to `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` in a strictly additive way.

Parent: LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB — the before/after measurement AC2 requires and the
AC4 re-measurement. Today the 916-skip / 336-free-GPU baseline was derived with
ad-hoc log greps, so the fix cannot be verified by the same invocation shape.

## Target outcome

One tool invocation reports, over any window, the abandonment → ghost →
cooldown chain: `saturated` without live work, cooldown skips in total, per
session, for `herdr-*` sessions, and how many of those skips happened while the
proxy's own nearest status poll said the GPU was free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report gains a **new** additive block (e.g. `prefill_thrash_cooldown`)
  containing at minimum: total `routing_skip_local … reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`
  skips, distinct skipped sessions, skips for `herdr-*` sessions and their
  distinct session count, and skips whose nearest preceding status poll within
  120 s has `local_in_flight_requests=0` **and** `slots_detail_stale=false`
  (with the sub-count where that poll reads `capacity_hint=idle`).
- The free-GPU attribution rule is exactly the one recorded in the parent's
  Appendix (nearest fresh poll within 120 s), and the rule is stated in the
  report itself so the number is not a magic constant.
- **Strictly additive**: every existing metric keeps its name, definition and
  JSON shape (`saturated_without_live_work`, the hint histogram, stale rate,
  downtime-dispatch counts, existing CSV artefacts). Existing consumers
  (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK, the nightly report) must parse the new output unchanged.
- The new block is emitted in both the human render and `--json`, and any new
  per-event CSV is written only as an *additional* file.
- Missing/gzipped/rotated log handling and window/coverage-gap semantics for the
  new metric match the existing ones — a coverage gap is reported as a gap, not
  as zero skips.
- If the cooldown release log line from the implementation item is present in
  the window, releases are counted by reason; when it is absent (older logs) the
  metric reads zero rather than failing.
- Unit tests cover the parsing, the attribution rule, the coverage-gap
  behaviour, and that the existing metric shapes are unchanged.
- The full project test suite passes with the change, run through the test
  skill (parent AC6; the dev-push gate enforces the full suite).

## Minimal implementation

- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`: a `analyse_prefill_thrash_skips()`
  pass over the same line stream, a `prefill_thrash_cooldown` report block, and
  render support; reuse the existing `_status_fields` / `_in_window` helpers.
- Nearest-poll attribution: index the status polls by timestamp once and bisect,
  rather than rescanning per skip.
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`: extend with the new
  fixtures (skip lines, interleaved status polls, gz rotation) and the
  additive-shape assertions.

## Deliverables

- Additive metric + tests, proven on the existing baseline window shape.
- A short note in the parent item giving the exact invocation used, so the AC4
  re-measurement uses the identical shape.

## Dependencies

None (the metric parses log lines that exist today). It must land **before**
the re-measurement item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (read-only reference for the skip log line and its fields)

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I want a session that owns a local slot to log its
**measured** reusable prefix at admission (AC1), so a cold-prefill admission is
visible in the log before it becomes a 120 s deadline cancellation and AC4 rule
(a) becomes evaluable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Measured prefix at admission.** When a session owns a local slot,
  `routing_resident_prefix` logs a **numeric** `n_past_actual` and the derived
  `reuse_ratio` (`min(n_past_actual, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens`),
  sourced from the best available measurement — here the `measured_prefill`
  store's last dispatch `total` for that `(model, session)` pair — and labelled
  `residency_source=measured_last_dispatch` so provenance is auditable against
  the live-snapshot `measured` source.
- **Rung order preserved.** `measured` (live `context_tokens`) still wins;
  `measured_last_dispatch` is consulted before the `session_slot` sentinel rung;
  `non_resident` / `unknown` are unchanged.
- **Provenance is auditable in the log.** The emitted line gains an **additive**
  `measurement=` field immediately after `residency_source=`; this item emits
  `measurement=measured` for both measured sources. All existing keys keep their
  relative order and `reuse_ratio=none` remains the numeric-absent form.
- **The gate uses the measurement.** Admission pricing reads the measured
  `n_past_actual` (`min(n_past_actual, estimated_tokens)` reusable) instead of the
  implicit "all tokens reused" assumption, so `reuse_ratio` is a real number and
  a grown prompt can now be denied with `resident_prefix_insufficient` — this is
  the intended AC4 rule (a) signal, not a regression; `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0`
  remains the documented rollback.
- **Fail-open, no fabrication.** `total` of `None`/`0`/non-finite, a missing store
  entry, an unreadable config, or any exception degrades to the existing
  `session_slot` behaviour; nothing raises into the request path and no
  synchronous `/slots` call is added (LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC).
- **Tests.** The xfail markers added by `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` for AC3(i) are
  removed and pass; `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` stays
  green under the changed-scope gate (AC7).
- **Model plumbed.** `_should_skip_local` passes `model_name` into
  `resolve_resident_prefix` (it is not a parameter today), defaulting to `None`
  for existing call sites so behaviour without a model name is unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `model_name: str | None = None` to `resolve_resident_prefix` and thread it
   from the `_should_skip_local` call site (and the reserve/pricing call site if
   present).
2. Add `RESIDENCY_SOURCE_MEASURED_LAST_DISPATCH = "measured_last_dispatch"` and
   include it in `ResidentPrefixFacts.resident`.
3. Insert the new rung between the `context_tokens` rung and the ownership rung,
   guarded by live ownership and `capture_enabled(server_config)` (read lazily and
   fail-open).
4. Add `measurement` to `ResidentPrefixFacts` (default `measured` for measured
   sources) and emit it from `_log_residency_decision`; keep the numeric-absent
   suppression for `None` `n_past_actual`.
5. Remove the AC3(i) xfail marker.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`
- `proxy/proxy/residency.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` (failing-first tests).

## Deliverables

- New ladder rung with auditable provenance, additive `measurement=` grammar, and
  green regression tests.

## Goal

As the verification agent, I want every decision that *cannot* be measured to
say **why** in a closed vocabulary (AC2), so "the ladder cannot measure" is
distinguishable from "there is no slot to measure" and AC4's unmeasured share is
attributable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — Unmeasured is explicit and distinguishable.** A decision that cannot
  be measured logs an explicit, closed-vocabulary reason — exactly one
  `measurement=` value per line, drawn from module-level constants: `measured`,
  `unavailable:no_slot`, `unavailable:no_prior_measurement`,
  `unavailable:stale_view`, `unavailable:capture_disabled`.
- **Precedence is deterministic.** `capture_disabled` (the
  `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled` rollback is off) wins over
  `no_prior_measurement` for a slot-owning session; `no_slot` applies to the
  fresh-view non-resident rung; `stale_view` applies to the `unknown` source
  where the residency view is absent/stale (extending `LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM`); a
  measured source always reports `measured`.
- **No fabricated numbers.** A non-measurement never logs a numeric
  `reuse_ratio` — the internal `0.0`/`1.0` gate sentinels are never surfaced, and
  the LP-0MVNPZY22008B536 regression (no `reuse_ratio=0.0000` for a session with
  no measurement) stays pinned by its existing test.
- **Backward compatible.** `reuse_ratio=none` is still emitted for every
  non-measurement, `residency_source` values are unchanged, and existing
  assertions/parsers keep working with no change.
- **Fail-open.** An unreadable config or store is treated as enabled/absent, not
  an error; the reason string never raises into the request path.
- **Tests.** The AC3(ii)/(iii) xfail markers from `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` are
  removed and pass; a table-driven test covers every vocabulary value's trigger;
  suite green under the changed-scope gate (AC7).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the vocabulary constants and a `measurement_reason(...)` helper (or
   equivalent derivation inside `resolve_resident_prefix`) so every return path
   sets exactly one reason.
2. Set `ResidentPrefixFacts.measurement` on all four ladder rungs, using
   `capture_enabled(server_config)` for `capture_disabled`.
3. Emit the field from `_log_residency_decision` (added by the measurement-rung
   child) and keep the numeric suppression rule.
4. Remove the AC3(ii)/(iii) xfail markers and add the table-driven vocabulary
   test.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` (failing-first tests).

## Deliverables

- Closed, documented unmeasured-reason vocabulary with deterministic precedence

## Goal

As the operator, I want a captured measurement to be **invalidated** when the
session loses its slot, the slot is reassigned to another session, or the model
changes, so the fix cannot trade one fabricated ratio for another (AC2/AC3(iv),
the parent item's highest risk).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Eviction clears.** Every reclaim chokepoint that emits `local_eviction`
  (`router_helpers._record_local_eviction`) clears the
  `(model, session)` measurement for the evicted session, so its next admission
  logs `unavailable:no_prior_measurement` rather than a stale ratio.
- **Slot release/reassignment clears.** `session._free_slot_assignment`
  (used by the lease reclaim and orphan-cleanup paths) clears the session's
  measurement, so a slot reassigned to another session cannot inherit the
  previous owner's prefix size.
- **Model switch does not reuse.** A measurement recorded under model A is never
  read for a dispatch on model B (the store is keyed by model, and the rung reads
  only the request's model); an explicit clear on the model-switch path is added
  where the switch is observable, with the key-scoped lookup as the backstop.
- **Live-ownership guard.** The rung only fires while `_session_owns_slot`
  returns a slot id; a measurement whose session no longer owns a slot is not
  used even if the clear path was missed.
- **AC3(iv) tests pass.** The invalidation fixtures from `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1`
  (eviction, reassignment, model switch) have their xfail markers removed and
  pass, each asserting no numeric `reuse_ratio` is emitted after invalidation.
- **Fail-open.** Clearing never raises and never changes a non-residency
  decision; no extra `/slots` query and no lock held across a dispatch.
- **AC7 — Suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the change
  (enforced by the dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs) — including the
  store-cap behaviour and the existing measured-prefill capture tests.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Give `clear_measured_prefill` its first real callers: in
   `_record_local_eviction`, in `session._free_slot_assignment`, and on the
   model-switch path (whatever `(model, session)` pair is losing its slot/model).
2. Have `clear_measured_prefill` accept a `None` model to clear **all** models for
   a session (single-pass over the dict), so call sites that do not know the
   model do not leave orphans.
3. Keep the rung's live-ownership guard as the backstop for a missed clear.
4. Remove the AC3(iv) xfail markers and extend the store clear tests.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_capture.py`

## Deliverables

- Measurement invalidation on eviction, slot release and model switch, with
  per-path regression tests.

## Goal

As the future investigator, I want the usage report's residency section to show
measured vs unmeasured-by-reason counts (AC4), so "decisions logged but all
unmeasured" is a visible finding instead of a silent zero.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC4 — Usage report reflects the split.** `analyze_proxy_usage.py` parses the
  new `measurement=` field (`RE_MEASUREMENT`, `LogEvent.measurement`) and its
  `## Residency-aware admission` section reports the measured/unmeasured counts
  plus a per-reason unmeasured breakdown table, so "decisions logged but all
  unmeasured" is a visible finding rather than a silent zero.
- **Parser compatibility.** New lines yield the literal reason; old lines (no
  field) yield `measurement is None`; `reuse_ratio=none` still maps to `None` and
  no existing field changes.
- **All-unmeasured finding.** When every decision in the window is unmeasured
  (the 3607/0 condition this item exists to fix), the section renders an explicit
  finding line naming the dominant reason.
- **Backward compatible aggregation.** Old-format log files parse to the same
  existing counters and the section renders as before; `aggregation` totals for
  `residency_events` are unchanged (new keys additive only).
- **Downstream handoff.** The per-reason counts are exposed in a form
  `LP-0MVQ4X1S30034BQ1`'s classifier can read (documented in the section's
  docstring), so AC4 rule (a) attribution is computable from the report.
- **Tests.** The xfail markers from `LP-0MVT2PF1C008LAPB` are removed and pass;
  no ad-hoc full-suite run (AC7 via the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `RE_MEASUREMENT` and the `LogEvent.measurement` field; populate it in the
   `routing_resident_prefix` branch.
2. Count `Counter(ev.measurement or "unrecorded")` over unmeasured decisions in
   `_append_residency_section` and render a compact reason table.
3. Emit the all-unmeasured finding when `measured == 0 and residency_events`.
4. Remove the xfail markers and keep the old-format fixture assertion.
